Alice.summary: B is better than A because migrants from A are better off and original residents of B are not worse off.

Bob.summary: C is better than B because C has complete equality and higher average welfare than B.

Charlie.summary: A is better than C because average welfare is higher in A than in C, despite lower total welfare.

c1.text: In world A, 100 million people live, each enjoying a welfare level of 100 units.

c2.text: In world B, 100 million migrants from A enjoy 105 units each, and 10 billion original inhabitants continue to enjoy 5 units each.

c3.text: In world C, all 10.1 billion inhabitants enjoy a welfare level of 10 units each.

c4.text: The people who migrated from A to B now have a higher level of welfare than when they lived in A.

c5.text: The remaining people in B continue to enjoy their worthwhile welfare level of 5 units each.

c6.text: World B is better than world A.

c7.text: In C, there is complete equality.

c8.text: The average welfare in C is higher than in B.

c9.text: World C is better than world B.

c10.text: The total sum of welfare is greater in C than in A.

c11.text: The average welfare is higher in A than in C.

c12.text: World A is better than world C.

h1.text: A world with less inequality is considered a better world.

h2.text: World A has complete equality while world B has inequality, so A has less inequality than B.

h3.text: World A is better than world B.

h4.text: World C has complete equality while world B has inequality, so C has less inequality than B.

h5.text: Worlds A and C are equally egalitarian, both having complete equality.

h6.text: World A has complete equality while world B has inequality, and average welfare is higher in A than in B.

h7.text: World A is better than world B.

h8.text: A world with a higher average welfare is considered a better world.

h9.text: The average welfare is higher in A than in B.

h10.text: World A is better than world B.

h11.text: A world with a greater total welfare is considered a better world.

h12.text: The total sum of welfare is greater in C than in B.

h13.text: World C is better than world A.

a.note: Under the less inequality criterion, A is better than B (denying Alice's conclusion), while C is better than B (consistent with Bob's conclusion).

b.note: Applying Bob's criteria (equality and higher average welfare), Bob concludes A is better than C (agreeing with Charlie), but concludes A is better than B, not B is better than A (disagreeing with Alice).

c.note: Under higher average welfare, A is better than B, so Alice's thesis is denied. Under greater total welfare, C is better than B (Bob's thesis is not denied) and C is better than A (Charlie's thesis is denied).
